reason: The laws fix the result in full. KeepsPrefix gives r ++ t. AddsAllAbsent, AddsOnlyAbsent and CountsAbsent make t hold exactly one row per absent starter id, with the same id, adapter and model. KeepsStarterOrder then fixes the order. NewDisabled, LockedDisabled and EnableKeepsState fix the enabled flag in every case, so two designs that pass give one registry.
